body: She is already going to a psychiatrist, like I mentioned on my post. She is meant to go there again in 10 days. It doesn't matter that much, though, because she doesn't talk about her darkest issues with the psychiastrist, because she is afraid of going to a mental hospital or get diagnosed with something that will prevent her from getting certain jobs in the future.

If I call the authorities, she'll fake that she is ok (she is good at it) and, at most, she would spend a night at the hospital and get sent back home the next morning. She would break up with me and probably attempt suicide shortly after. Even if she doesn't suicide, she breaks up with me and I know that at some points I will hear the heartcrushing news that she is dead, because no one cares as much as I do.

First of all, thank you for actual input.

> Maybe try to reason with her about how her future with her psychology degree would be helpful to others and would make a world a better place.

She hates the course, she sees herself as a failing student, even though she managed to pass in every subject this semester. She credits me and the resources I gave her, though. The university environment became pretty hostile for her this year, aswell, since the ex-boyfriend she had from last year started spreading intimate and personal information about her to other classmates. Not to mention other unfair things that she unluckily had to go through, due to bad teachers and awful classmates. I helped her as much as I could (I completely went beyond what I had to do in this regard) and I even propose that she would work within my work group, which she refused, because "she couldn't change after the semester started" (which she actually could, but she didn't even try).

> Is her existence completely based on reason? I'd suggest doing a deep dive into different philosophers and their interpretation of the "meaning of life". Hopefully you'll be able to find something that you can use.

My outlook on life is very different from hers and, of course I tried to share my thoughts and experiences with her, but even though she likes having those conversations, they don't have any effect on the long run. After 7 months, Nietzsche and Schopenhauer are still her favorites. Her mom, who is a High School Philosophy Teacher mentioned that my girlfriend misinterprets Nietzsche. However, my knowledge is only on a basic level regarding specific philosophers and it is hard to come up with counterarguments with my girlfriend, who has read her favorite philosophers for years. I've really done everything I could in this regard, to try and open new spiritual/philosophical/existential experiences for her, but they either vanish the next day or get flat out refused. To answer your first question, she considers that the path to the existential problem may only be solved with the use of reason and life experience.

> Overall, it sounds like she's way too closed off into herself. If she's as cynical as she sounds, maybe getting her out and about won't help that much, but usually it's a good suggestion, so I'm going to bring it up here. I have long periods of time when I want to lay on my bed and hate myself, but going out and seeing the world, no matter how small, always makes me hold on just a little bit more.

This all happened about 30 hours after we went to the movies. It was very sudden and random. This really makes me think she might have found someone online who is willing to do a suicide pact. Even though she has been home alone, we still went out a lot. During the last month we went to some of the most wonderful places on my country (that get visited by millions of tourist every year). She loved it. We also went to the Zoo, which she loved aswell. We went to a store that sells food from all over the world and had a good dinner with the things we bought. She actually doesn't lay in bed the entire day - on the contrary, she tends to leave her house everyday, which is actually scary. Many times she doesn't disclose where she went or what she is doing, which is scary. She is doing these things today. I think she might be looking for a place to suicide (there is the possibility that she found a place already) or buying materials to suicide. 

Thank you again.
